findings.title: 9/14 'double charge' was one settled payment + one released authorization, not a duplicate
findings.explanation: TX-9001 is the real settled payment for INV-2609 ($149, September Vault renewal). TX-9002 was a card authorization that hit capture_timeout and was released back to the customer's card on 9/18, unfunded. Per POL-B-AUTH, released/unfunded authorizations are not refundable and were never actual charges. The customer was only charged once. SUP-5601 agent S-22 incorrectly concluded this was a 'duplicate charge' and promised a $149 refund - that commitment was not warranted by the facts and should be withdrawn.

findings.title: Deep Time Analytics $30 add-on was validly added by an admin seat
findings.explanation: The add-on was added 2026-09-12 by U-2, an admin-level seat on the account. Per POL-B-ADD, admin seats are permitted to add add-ons, which then bill separately starting at the next renewal - exactly what happened (started 9/14, billed as a separate $30 line item on INV-2609-AO). This matches policy and is not a billing error, though the account owner may not have been personally aware of the change made by another admin.

findings.title: July proration charge (INV-2607P, $59.60) correctly computed
findings.explanation: The $59.60 charge equals 12/30 days at the $149/mo Vault rate (149 * 12/30 = 59.60), matching proration policy exactly for the plan upgrade effective 2026-07-02.

findings.title: Unused-time credit CR-778 ($19.60) was correctly issued but never applied or disclosed to the owner, violating credit policy
findings.explanation: When the customer upgraded plans on 2026-07-02, a $19.60 credit for unused time on the prior ('Shelf') plan was correctly generated (CR-778, source INV-2607P). However, auto-apply was disabled on this account and the credit was never applied to a subsequent invoice; owner_notified is still false. Per POL-B-CRD v2, unapplied credits older than 30 days with auto-apply disabled must be flagged to the account owner and applied/refunded per their instruction - this never happened (credit is now several months old). Compounding the issue, when the customer directly asked about this exact charge on 2026-08-06 (SUP-5549), agent S-22 told them 'no credit due,' which was factually incorrect since CR-778 already existed at that time.

findings.title: INV-2602 $44 charge correctly reflects a $5 goodwill credit
findings.explanation: INV-2602 shows a $49 plan charge with a $5 goodwill credit (CR-512, from SUP-5201) applied, netting to $44. This is correctly recorded and applied - not an error.

corrections.prior_claim: S-22 concluded the two $149 entries on 9/14 were a duplicate charge and promised the customer a $149 refund within 5-7 business days.
corrections.corrected_claim: Only one of the two $149 entries was an actual charge (TX-9001, settled payment for INV-2609). The other (TX-9002) was a card authorization that timed out and was released unfunded on 9/18. There was no duplicate charge, and per POL-B-AUTH the released authorization is not refundable. The promised $149 refund should be withdrawn.

corrections.prior_claim: S-22 told the customer there was 'no credit due' regarding the July 2 prorated $59.60 upgrade charge.
corrections.corrected_claim: A $19.60 unused-time credit (CR-778) tied to that exact charge/invoice (INV-2607P) had already been issued on 2026-07-02, before this ticket was even opened. The customer was owed a credit, and the prior answer was incorrect. The credit remains unapplied and should now be surfaced and applied/refunded per the customer's instruction.

Should SUP-5601 and SUP-5602 tickets be formally updated/closed to reflect the corrected conclusions (no duplicate charge, refund commitment withdrawn, credit issue identified)?
Should there be a process fix to ensure credits with auto-apply disabled are proactively flagged to owners once they cross the 30-day threshold (to prevent recurrence of the CR-778 situation)?
Does the account owner want to keep or remove the Deep Time Analytics add-on now that its origin (admin seat U-2) has been clarified?
